title: Benchmark launches consultation on increasing publishing frequency of synthetic and natural graphite price grades to every two weeks
gist: Benchmark Mineral Intelligence proposes moving its natural and synthetic graphite price assessments from monthly to every two weeks starting 10 December 2026, with feedback due by 6 December. It cites rising liquidity, ex-China supply chain growth, fast-moving export controls, tariffs and anti-dumping measures, higher price volatility, and more contracts indexed to its prices.

insights.claim: Benchmark says liquidity and transaction volumes across the graphite and anode supply chain have risen steadily and expects this to continue, with supply chains outside China growing and buyers signing more offtakes to diversify sources.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Ex-China graphite supply buildout is gaining transactional traction, supporting non-Chinese anode material developers.

insights.claim: Producers, anode makers, cell manufacturers, automakers and financial institutions are increasingly writing contracts linked to Benchmark's graphite indices, driving demand for a more frequent price reference.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Graphite is financializing toward index-linked pricing, which can enable hedging and better price transparency.
insights.locator: Industry need for a more frequent reference

insights.claim: Benchmark says export controls, tariffs and anti-dumping measures on graphite and anode materials can move prices and trade patterns within weeks, which a monthly assessment cycle can miss or report late.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Trade policy is a primary short-term price driver for battery graphite, raising geopolitical risk for anode supply chains.
insights.quote: A monthly cycle can miss these moves or report them late.

insights.claim: Prices across flake, spherical and synthetic graphite now move faster in response to anode demand, production changes and inventory shifts, according to Benchmark.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Higher graphite volatility increases input-cost risk for battery makers and EV OEMs.

insights.claim: Benchmark proposes publishing all natural and synthetic graphite prices every two weeks at 4:00pm UK time on alternate Thursdays, starting Thursday 10 December 2026, with market feedback invited by 6 December 2026.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Faster price discovery will tighten the reference for graphite-linked contracts from December 2026.

insights.claim: The change covers flake graphite grades FOB China, CIF North America, DDP China and FOB East Africa, uncoated spherical graphite (10, 15, 25 µm), needle coke and petroleum coke grades DDP China, and graphitisation tolling fees.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Inclusion of East Africa and North America grades shows ex-China price points are becoming established benchmarks.
